evidence.note: HEAD content-length wrong and V2-vs-V4 presigned mismatch: diagnosed the actual causes (Flask overriding Content-Length; boto3 default V2 signing) rather than blindly patching symptoms.

boto3 rejected signatures for special-char keys (SignatureDoesNotMatch). Agent traced it to using Flask's URL-decoded path, reasoned about S3 canonical-URI encoding rules, and revised the SigV4 design to consume the raw encoded REQUEST_URI without re-encoding — a foundational signing assumption falsified and corrected, then re-verified ('Special characters now work').
After fixes, re-ran the full boto3 test suite on fresh instances to confirm the correction held and dependents didn't regress.
Concurrency test passed on first attempt — no storage/locking assumption was falsified, so no pivot was required there (bounds the opportunity for correction).

reasoning: The agent treated verification failures as signal about the design: when boto3 falsified its SigV4 path-handling assumption, it diagnosed the root cause and revised the canonical-URI design rather than surface-patching, then re-verified (anchor 8). Other issues (HEAD, presigned) were also fixed at the cause level. It falls short of 10 because corrections were reactive rather than proactively de-risked, and the mostly-smooth build offered few foundational divergences to pivot on.
